set.typical_award_size: Not a direct subsidy. Prohousing status gives bonus points or set-asides in state AHSC, IIG, MHP and PLHA competitive rounds and eligibility for Prohousing Incentive Program grants. The City was designated in November 2022 and the designation was valid until January 2026; the City circulated a draft renewal application in November 2025 (public review now closed). HCD's Prohousing Application Tracker lists the City's renewal application as received June 12, 2026 with status Pending Revisions, and HCD's designated jurisdictions list as of August 10, 2026 shows San Diego County and Chula Vista but not the City of San Diego.
set.cycle_notes: Renewal application received by HCD June 12, 2026; status Pending Revisions on the HCD tracker. Designation lapsed January 2026 pending renewal.
set.next_deadline: No deadline; renewal application pending at HCD (status Pending Revisions as of November 8, 2026). Check the HCD designated jurisdictions list before claiming Prohousing points in a 2027 state application.

reason: City page and HCD list match the record; HCD tracker adds that the renewal application was received June 12, 2026 and is Pending Revisions.

set.typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Ordinance 24-OR0004-1 (approved by Council February 10, 2024) raised the applicability threshold from three or more units to ten or more units, raised the set-aside for low and moderate income households from 10 percent to 15 percent, and added unit mix, dispersal and equal amenity requirements for reserved units in multifamily projects; rental projects have been covered since the September 9, 2020 Phase 1 amendment. Coastal Commission staff (report dated January 22, 2026, hearing February 5, 2026, item LCP-6-OCN-25-0030-2) recommended certification only with modifications that set the threshold at seven or more units, add an acutely low income category, require 55 year rental and resale restrictions, and let ADUs satisfy the requirement in any residential project; the report states the City agrees to the modifications. The Commission's final action was not confirmed. In-lieu fee is calculated per square foot (Housing Element Program 3) and may be deferred on the same terms as impact fees; fees must be used for low and moderate income housing. A further Chapter 14C revision was noticed for a May 6, 2026 hearing; outcome not confirmed.
set.next_deadline: Applies at entitlement. Confirm whether the Coastal Commission certified LCP-6-OCN-25-0030-2 with the seven unit threshold, whether the May 6, 2026 Chapter 14C revisions were adopted, and the current in-lieu fee rate with the Housing Division.
set.audit_note: Threshold corrected from three units to ten (citywide ordinance) and seven (Coastal staff recommendation). ci.oceanside.ca.us returns 403 and Oceanside has no Legistar API client, so adoption status could not be confirmed.

reason: Coastal staff report shows the 2024 ordinance raised the threshold to ten units (seven recommended by Coastal staff), not three, which changes which projects are covered.

set.typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Housing Element Program 2 commits the City to amend its density bonus ordinance (Zoning Ordinance Article 30) within one year of adoption to conform to AB 1763, SB 1227 and AB 2345. State law (as amended by AB 1287, effective January 1, 2024) allows up to a 100 percent bonus for projects reserving at least 15 percent of base units for very low income, 24 percent for lower income or 44 percent for moderate income households. In the coastal zone, Coastal Commission staff note that the certified Article 30 density bonus provisions do not apply to the Downtown District; the City's Downtown amendment (Ordinance 23-OR0749-1, LCP-6-OCN-25-0029-2) sets an 86 units per acre base density and staff recommended allowing State density bonuses there and requiring the City to submit updated density bonus regulations by January 1, 2029. In-lieu fee deferral on the same terms as impact fee deferral is available for inclusionary obligations.
set.next_deadline: Applies at entitlement. Confirm the current Zoning Ordinance Article 30 text, whether the Coastal Commission certified the Downtown density amendment, and any 2026 amendments with Planning.
set.audit_note: Removed unverified claim about the City's density bonus application form; Coastal staff tie the 15/24/44 percent tiers to State law and the Downtown amendment, not to the inclusionary ordinance.

reason: Coastal staff report shows certified density bonus provisions do not apply in the Downtown District pending an LCP update due by 2029, which the record omitted.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: DIR Public Works Case No. 2006-001 (citing PW 2004-016, Rancho Santa Fe) holds that conduit tax-exempt bond financing is not payment out of public funds under Labor Code 1720(b) because proceeds never enter public coffers; any City loan or land layered with the bonds must be assessed separately (https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2007/2006-001.pdf).

reason: Housing Element matches Program 1 and a DIR coverage determination states conduit bond financing alone does not trigger prevailing wage; issuance policy and fees still unconfirmed.

set.typical_award_size: Gap loans from the Low and Moderate Income Housing Asset Fund (former CDC loans, rents, note repayments and interest; $1,203,205 deposited in FY 2023-24). Available funds were $9,709,773 as of July 1, 2023 (after $38.9M loans receivable and $0.9M land), and the SB 341 report shows an excess surplus of $4,375,086. Recent commitments: $1,000,000 to Veterans Village (54 units, 2019 RFP) and $4,000,000 to Valley Senior Village (50 units, 25 for homeless households, loan agreement December 6, 2021, complete). Funds are awarded through periodic City RFPs; the FY 2023-24 report says the City intended to release an RFP in FY 2025 pairing SHA funds with $1.5 million of HOME-ARP. Housing Element Program 2.8 lists Recycled RDA Funds with LIHTC, CalCHA bonds, CalHFA, CalHome, PLHA and HOME.
set.cycle_notes: Periodic RFPs rather than a fixed annual round (March 2019, March 2020; RFP planned for FY 2024-25 with HOME-ARP). The City's HOME page says development funds are released through periodic RFPs.
set.next_deadline: No open round as of November 8, 2026. Watch for the next Housing and Neighborhood Services RFP; a HOME substantial amendment for Valley Creek Apartments (136 senior units) was noticed for March 25, 2026.
set.audit_note: SB 341 report link on the City page returns 404; the FY 2023-24 report was opened directly at DocumentCenter/View/7844.

reason: SB 341 report shows SHA funds are awarded through periodic RFPs with about $9.7M available and a $4.4M excess surplus, not case by case without a NOFA.
